title: Just-in-Time Batching Advisor: compact guidance and inline savings timeline
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Design a compact, inline advisor that surfaces "just-in-time" batching and cache recommendations directly inside the route configuration and rollout screens. The feature should show an interactive 'cost momentum' mini-graph that predicts short-term token spend and latency impact given a candidate batching/prefill policy, provide one-click safe presets, and surface guardrail warnings for user-facing regressions (e.g., latency spike, quality risk, or customer SLA violation). The advisor is intended for PM/engineer users who want rapid, low-friction guidance during a rollout without leaving the route or rollout context.
background: We have many large, modal-heavy batch/cache wizards that are useful but interruptive. Multiple customers told us they want quick suggestions when tuning a route during a canary or A/B rollout. This ticket explores a compact, in-context advisor that offers instant estimates and safe apply/preview paths. It leans on existing backend evaluation signals (simulated throughput, historical latencies) and the Optimize engine's recommendation API.
acceptance_criteria: Compact advisor component appears in Route Settings and Rollout details panels
Advisor displays three suggestion tiers (Conservative, Balanced, Aggressive) with estimated per-minute token savings and median latency delta
Mini 'cost momentum' chart updates in response to slider or preset selection and matches backend simulator within 5% for canonical workloads
Apply Preset performs a dry-run preview in the rollout timeline and creates a reversible change that supports immediate rollback
Guardrail warnings are clearly visible and include suggested mitigations with links to deeper config pages
Design passes accessibility checklist: keyboard navigable, color contrast AA, screen reader labels for the chart and controls
Prototype (Figma) validated in at least two user interviews with PM/engineer personas and feedback incorporated
notes: Key trade-offs: keep the surface minimal (no full simulator modal) vs. accuracy of the estimate. We will prioritize conservative defaults for production routes and allow engineers to opt into aggressive presets during internal experimentation. We might later expose an 'explain' link that launches the full batch/cache playground for power users.
decisions: Show three pre-set tiers rather than arbitrary sliders to reduce cognitive load
Inline mini-chart will use a condensed sparkline + hover details to keep height under 72px
Apply action will create a reversible route patch in the rollout engine rather than mutating the live config directly
user_research_findings: Early interviews preferred a timeline view that shows cost impact over the next 15 minutes instead of aggregate daily savings
PMs favored explicit rollback affordances over optimistic 'apply immediately' flows
Engineers want a text-only summary that can be copy-pasted into incident tickets or PR descriptions
accessibility_considerations: Ensure chart has ARIA labels and textual fallback summary
All controls reachable by keyboard; presets tabbable and have focus styles
Color palette to remain WCAG AA compliant; do not rely on color alone for warnings
risks: Estimates could be misinterpreted as guarantees; need microcopy to explain uncertainty
Backend simulator service (optimize-sim) might not cover edge-case workloads leading to poor guidance
Over-simplifying presets could accidentally push customers into quality regressions without clear safeguards
mitigations: Add confidence band and short copy: 'estimated range based on recent traffic patterns'
Default to conservative preset for routes with high traffic or SLA tags
Surface quick link to full evaluation report and sample prompt fail-cases in the rollout details
